    24→---
    25→
    26→# VEX Language Fundamentals
    27→
    28→VEX (Vector EXpression) is Houdini's high-performance shading and geometry manipulation language. It compiles to native code and runs in parallel across points, primitives, vertices, or detail.
    29→
    30→## Execution Contexts
    31→
    32→VEX runs inside **wrangle nodes** (Attribute Wrangle, Volume Wrangle, etc.) or **VOP networks** that compile down to VEX.
    33→
    34→| Context | Wrangle Node | Runs Over | Variables Available |
    35→|---------|-------------|-----------|-------------------|
    36→| SOP | Attribute Wrangle | Points, Prims, Vertices, Detail | `@ptnum`, `@numpt`, `@primnum`, `@numprim` |
    37→| DOP | Gas Field Wrangle | Voxels | `@ix`, `@iy`, `@iz`, `@resx`, `@resy`, `@resz` |
    38→| CHOP | Channel Wrangle | Samples | `@C`, `@I`, `@Time` |
    39→| COP | Pixel Wrangle | Pixels | `@IX`, `@IY`, `@RESX`, `@RESY` |
    40→
    41→**Run-over modes** (SOP context):
    42→- **Points** (default) -- code runs once per point, `@ptnum` is current point index
    43→- **Primitives** -- code runs once per prim, `@primnum` is current prim index
    44→- **Vertices** -- code runs once per vertex, `@vtxnum` is current vertex index
    45→- **Detail** -- code runs once for entire geometry (global operations)
    46→
    47→## Data Types
    48→
    49→```vex
    50→// Scalar types
    51→int i = 42;
    52→float f = 3.14;
    53→string s = "hello";
    54→
    55→// Vector types
    56→vector2 uv = {0.5, 0.5};          // 2 floats (u, v)
    57→vector pos = {1.0, 2.0, 3.0};     // 3 floats (x, y, z)
    58→vector4 q = {0, 0, 0, 1};         // 4 floats (quaternion/homogeneous)
    59→
    60→// Matrix types
    61→matrix2 m2 = ident();             // 2x2
    62→matrix3 m3 = ident();             // 3x3 (rotation/scale)
    63→matrix  m4 = ident();             // 4x4 (full transform)
    64→
    65→// Arrays
    66→int nums[] = {1, 2, 3};
    67→float vals[] = array(0.1, 0.2);
    68→string names[] = {"a", "b"};
    69→vector pts[] = {};                 // Empty vector array
    70→```
    71→
    72→## Type Prefixes (@-binding)
    73→
    74→When reading/writing geometry attributes via `@` shorthand, prefix declares type:
    75→
    76→| Prefix | Type | Example | Default If New |
    77→|--------|------|---------|----------------|
    78→| (none) | float | `@density` | 0.0 |
    79→| `f@` | float | `f@density` | 0.0 |
    80→| `i@` | int | `i@id` | 0 |
    81→| `v@` | vector | `v@velocity` | {0,0,0} |
    82→| `u@` | vector2 | `u@uv` | {0,0} |
    83→| `p@` | vector4 | `p@orient` | {0,0,0,0} |
    84→| `s@` | string | `s@name` | "" |
    85→| `2@` | matrix2 | `2@mtx` | identity |
    86→| `3@` | matrix3 | `3@transform` | identity |
    87→| `4@` | matrix | `4@xform` | identity |
    88→
    89→**Important**: The prefix is only needed on the **first use** of an attribute in your code. After that, VEX knows the type.
    90→
    91→## Control Flow
    92→
    93→```vex
    94→// Conditionals
    95→if (condition) {
    96→    // ...
    97→} else if (other) {
    98→    // ...
    99→} else {
   100→    // ...
   101→}
   102→
   103→// Ternary
   104→float val = condition ? a : b;
   105→
   106→// For loop
   107→for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
   108→    // ...
   109→}
   110→
   111→// Foreach (arrays)
   112→int pts[] = neighbours(0, @ptnum);
   113→foreach (int pt; pts) {
   114→    vector pos = point(0, "P", pt);
   115→}
   116→
   117→// While
   118→while (condition) {
   119→    // ...
   120→}
   121→
   122→// Break / Continue
   123→for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
   124→    if (skip_condition) continue;
   125→    if (done_condition) break;
   126→}
   127→```
   128→
   129→## Inputs and Outputs
   130→
   131→Wrangle nodes have up to 4 geometry inputs, accessed by index:
   132→
   133→```vex
   134→// Input 0 (default, wired to first input)
   135→vector pos = point(0, "P", @ptnum);
   136→
   137→// Input 1 (second input)
   138→vector target = point(1, "P", @ptnum);
   139→
   140→// Input 2, 3
   141→float val = prim(2, "density", @primnum);
   142→string name = detail(3, "name");
   143→```
   144→
   145→**Output**: Writing to `@attribute` modifies the output geometry. Point wrangle output is always input 0's geometry with modifications applied.
   146→
   147→## Preprocessor
   148→
   149→```vex
   150→// Include files
   151→#include <math.h>
   152→#include <voplib.h>
   153→
   154→// Defines
   155→#define PI 3.14159265
   156→#define TWO_PI (2.0 * PI)
   157→#define SQR(x) ((x) * (x))
   158→```
   159→
   160→## Functions
   161→
   162→```vex
   163→// User-defined functions (declared before main code)
   164→float remap(float val; float omin, omax, nmin, nmax) {
   165→    float t = clamp((val - omin) / (omax - omin), 0, 1);
   166→    return lerp(nmin, nmax, t);
   167→}
   168→
   169→// Overloaded by type
   170→vector remap(vector val; float omin, omax, nmin, nmax) {
   171→    return set(
   172→        remap(val.x, omin, omax, nmin, nmax),
   173→        remap(val.y, omin, omax, nmin, nmax),
   174→        remap(val.z, omin, omax, nmin, nmax)
   175→    );
   176→}
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Note**: VEX uses semicolons to separate parameter types in function signatures (not commas between same-type params).
   180→
   181→## VEX vs HScript Expressions
   182→
   183→| Feature | VEX (Wrangles) | HScript (Parameter Fields) |
   184→|---------|----------------|---------------------------|
   185→| Speed | Compiled, parallel | Interpreted, serial |
   186→| Geometry access | Full read/write | Read-only via `point()` |
   187→| Use case | Heavy processing | Simple parameter expressions |
   188→| Syntax | C-like | `$F`, `ch("parm")` |
   189→| Variables | `@P`, `@ptnum` | `$PT`, `$NPT` |
   190→
   191→**Rule of thumb**: If you need to process more than a few hundred points or modify geometry, use VEX. If you need a simple expression in a parameter field, HScript is fine.
   192→
